acceptance: Power, throughput and maintenance tests stop at the deadline, shown by tests.
No BenchBox-imposed execution timeout remains; user-set ones still work.
The before-and-after timing table is recorded, within 2% or approved by the owner.
description:
## Problem
After step 1 the deadline is checked between phases and between queries of the generic loop. Power, throughput and maintenance tests (benchbox/platforms/base/execution.py `_execute_*_test`, benchbox/core/throughput/runner.py, benchbox/core/tpcds and tpch test classes) do not yet see it. BenchBox also imposes execution limits of its own: the TPC-DS runner's `query_timeout` 300 s, checked only after the query returns (benchbox/core/tpcds/benchmark/runner.py), its `stream_timeout` 3600 s, `tpch/benchmark.py` `query_timeout` 300, and `execution.concurrent_queries.query_timeout_seconds` 300 with 600 and 180 in two presets (benchbox/cli/config.py).

## Owner decisions
Execution defaults: "remove them, in line with 'no default timeout'. The settings stay available for a user to set; they just have no value unless set. The after-the-fact check is deleted." Timing: "if the medians differ by more than 2%, I stop and bring you the numbers before arming. Otherwise I put the table in the pull request and continue." ('I' is the agent.) Source: owner's answer in the choice dialog, 2026-11-20.

## Change
1. Power, throughput and maintenance tests check the deadline between queries and between streams; the effective stream limit is the smaller of the user's stream setting and the time remaining; the existing stream cancel events are set when the deadline passes.
2. Where an adapter can cancel a running query (by search: GizmoSQL and Onehouse; confirm by reading each), pass it the time remaining.
3. Remove the BenchBox-imposed execution defaults listed above; each setting keeps working when a user sets it. Delete the after-the-fact check. Trace every reader of each default before removing it and list them in the pull request.
4. Result rows for queries not run because of the deadline are absent, not failed; the query in flight is recorded as timed out (the schema already allows status TIMEOUT).

## Decision gates
The deadline check is never inside a timed section; show the placement in the pull request. Timing proof: TPC-H SF 1 on DuckDB, power phase, five runs on develop and five on the branch, one at a time through `make heavy-run`, same machine, alternating if admission allows; compare the median of total query time. More than 2% apart: stop, do not arm, bring the table. If a removed default turns out to be relied on by a test tier or UAT config, list it and set it explicitly there; do not keep it as a product default. No change to how results are computed.

## Verification rubric
Pass, by tests that fail before the change: a power test with a stubbed slow query stops at the deadline and the result marks that query timed out and omits the rest; a throughput test sets the cancel events at the deadline and its effective limit is min(setting, remaining); a maintenance test stops between operations; with nothing set, a stubbed query that outlives 300 s and a stream that outlives 3600 s are not stopped or failed; a user-set stream limit still works; an adapter with native cancel receives the remaining time. The ten-run timing table with heavy-run log paths is in the pull request, or the item is blocked with the table. `make pr-preflight` exits 0.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking; `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job that never ran or was cancelled by the runner, never for a test that failed. Review threads: reply, and resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text the owner has not already chosen is shown to the owner before it is committed. No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment. A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`.
